title: Babur Reaches Punjab and Sends Daulat Khan to Guru Nanak

blocks.text: The narrative now moves into the Punjab campaign and evokes the Guru's own testimony against invasion with the line about Khurasan and Hindustan. As Babur takes Saidpur and pushes onward, the violence of empire is set beside the moral witness that will judge it.

Babur asks Daulat Khan to locate Guru Nanak near Eminabad and bring him into contact with the imperial camp. Even offers of land and favor are placed on the table, but the page makes clear that worldly inducements cannot measure the Guru's station.

When Daulat finally approaches, courtly status falls away. Daulat Khan dismounted and bowed at the Guru's feet, coming on foot before a presence that does not need armies, titles, or gifts to command obedience.
